It had drifted into three copies: the index query that decides suppression matched 10 words, while the inbound handler that reacts live and the instrumentation that attributes opt-outs each matched 5. Nobody went un-suppressed (the index re-derives from raw inbound bodies and is the real net), but STOPALL / REVOKE / OPT OUT produced no confirmation reply, no sms.opt_out compliance row, and stayed sendable until the 5-minute cache turned over 2026-09-23 OPT-OUT OVER-MATCH: the live unsubscribe rule in server/services/smsResponseParser.ts matched any reply that STARTS with a keyword, so a visit ('Stop by around 3?', 'stop over after work', 'End of the day works') silently unsubscribed the customer from every text. Only stop by/in/over/at/off and end of/up are now carved out and go to a person (they cannot be a revocation); every other reply opening with a keyword, punctuated or phrased ('Stop.', 'stop texting me'), still unsubscribes, since missing a real opt-out is the worse error. 2026-09-23 REVOCATION FIRST (audit item B): PATTERNS is first-hit and the opt-out rules sat after confirm/cancel/decline, so 'STOP. Cancel all texts' CANCELLED the booking and recorded no opt-out, and 'Stop texting me, too expensive' became a declined estimate. Revocation now runs first; a phrase rule catches explicit plain-English revocations ('cancel all texts', 'stop texting me', 'don't text me' incl. iOS curly apostrophes, 'no more texts', 'take me off your list', 'unsubscribe me'); the visit carve-outs are same-line only and narrowed, so 'Stop at once', 'stop off my list', 'End of discussion' and 'STOP' + a new line unsubscribe. A bare 'Cancel' stays cancel-appointment (consent-ledger design note F5 leaves it to counsel). 2026-09-24 P1 REVIEW HARDENING: negated revocations (for example 'Don't stop texting me', 'Never stop texting me', 'I do not want to unsubscribe') now route to a person with no autoAction, and remove/take language only opts out when it names an SMS/list object, so booking-scoped requests such as 'remove me from tomorrow's appointment' cannot become durable global SMS opt-outs. 2026-09-29 AUDIT F3: (1) a spoken do-not-call survives an SMS opt-in. YES opts in only an SMS-suppressed number, never a voice-only one; markPhoneOptedIn keeps opted_out=1 + VOICE for a do-not-call row and updates the caches from the row read back; a text STOP on a do-not-call row becomes SMS+VOICE (a full opt-out) so a later START falls back to VOICE, never to callable; START/UNSTOP/YES grant sms_* ledger scopes only (design rule 4), not 'all'. Before this, YES or STOP-then-START wrote opted_out=0 over a VOICE row, and the voice recovery/follow-up lanes could call a number that had said 'stop calling'. (2) Parser: 'stop at'/'stop off'/'end of' are allow-listed (once / my list / discussion...), so 'Stop at five ok?' and 'End of September is better' go to a person; 'Why did you stop texting me?', 'I'll stop texting you' and 'cancel text me when you have an opening' no longer unsubscribe (the last also no longer auto-cancels); the negated span is removed instead of the whole message, so 'You guys never stop texting me. STOP' unsubscribes.<br>tests: server/__tests__/smsOrchestrator.golden.test.ts (49): loadCustomerContext matched customers on LIKE '%'+last-10-digits with .limit(1) and no ORDER BY, so a shared household line, business number or recycled number resolved to a NON-DETERMINISTIC row. #988 feeds that row's name and vehicle into the drafter, and CONFIRM / CANCEL / estimate-approval replies MUTATE the booking, lead, callback and estimate selected by that same shared phone.
